claims.statement: The pasted conclusion X is isomorphic to A^1 is false for r>1; X=A^r is a literal counterexample.
claims.status: elementary dimension argument

claims.statement: Corrected affine-space cancellation fails for threefolds over every field of positive characteristic.
claims.status: known external theorem, not independently re-proved here

claims.statement: For complex X with X times A^1 isomorphic to A^4, X is isomorphic to A^3.
claims.status: open target; no proof or counterexample supplied

claims.statement: A characteristic-zero locally nilpotent derivation with slice s has B=(ker D)[s], and kernel is isomorphic to B/(s).
claims.status: standard lemma reconstructed in writing

claims.statement: A slice derivation on k^[4] in characteristic zero has polynomial kernel if it fixes an ambient coordinate.
claims.status: corollary of known external theorem plus reconstructed regularity argument

claims.statement: A slice az+bw+c over k[x,y] with an explicit Bezout identity au+bv=1 is a coordinate, giving cancellation for that subcase.
claims.status: elementary sufficient subcase with written proof and exact inverse identities

claims.statement: For D(v)=Nv+b in characteristic zero, D is locally nilpotent iff N is nilpotent; then a slice exists iff b is not in im N, and its kernel is polynomial.
claims.status: standard affine-linear case reconstructed by a written flow proof
claims.scope: companion verifies an explicit four-dimensional instance; not the universal theorem in a proof assistant

claims.statement: A slice projection can send an ambient coordinate to a nonconstant non-coordinate invariant.
claims.status: explicit counterexample to a proof shortcut, not to cancellation

claims.statement: Every nonlinear slice derivation on C^[4] fixes some ambient coordinate.
claims.status: unproved obligation equivalent here to the cancellation target; not an easier established result

claims.statement: The leading homogeneous part of a slice locally nilpotent derivation need not admit a slice.
claims.status: explicit counterexample to a proof shortcut, not to cancellation

claims.statement: A positively weighted homogeneous derivation with a polynomial slice has negative homogeneous degree and is triangular after ordering the variables by weight.
claims.status: elementary reconstructed observation; reduces the four-variable case to known positive results

claims.statement: For the specified Freudenburg derivation Delta and a in k[x,f], Delta+a*d/dw has a polynomial slice exactly when a is a nonzero constant, in characteristic zero.
claims.status: complete family-specific written proof; independently critiqued by another model
claims.scope: not a classification of arbitrary four-variable locally nilpotent derivations

claims.statement: For the same Delta and a in k[f,g], a slice exists exactly when a=c+fgP with c nonzero constant; all positive cases have explicit coordinate slices and polynomial kernels.
claims.status: complete family-specific written proof; independently critiqued by another model

claims.statement: For a=1+x an explicit Laurent-parameter orbit has polynomial endpoints but translation time 3/e^5, excluding every polynomial slice.
claims.status: written all-degree pole obstruction with independent standard-library identity checks

claims.statement: An invariant coordinate of a leading derivation need not lift, even to first order in a homogenizing parameter; positive-weight coordinate searches can miss solved nonlinear translations.
claims.status: explicit counterexamples to proposed methods, not to cancellation

claims.statement: The modified Makar-Limanov invariant equals the ordinary invariant when a slice exists, and does not distinguish the Russell cubic cylinder from affine four-space.
claims.status: known external theorem; novelty collision identified

claims.statement: Delta+(1+y)*d/dw has no polynomial slice; an algebraic-constant orbit certificate has polynomial endpoints and time (2/C)*H^(-13), with C^3=16/35.
claims.status: written all-degree proof, separate model audit, independent exact endpoint checks

claims.statement: In characteristic zero, any polynomial slice of total degree at most two is an ambient coordinate.
claims.status: elementary linear-algebra proof reconstructed; no novelty claimed

claims.statement: For the specified Delta and C=k[x,f,g], Delta(R) intersect C equals L(M), where L(P)=gP+2(xg-f^3)P_x and M=(f,g-x^5)C+x^2*k[f,g].
claims.status: complete working proof with separate model reconstruction and constructive exact classifier
claims.scope: specific derivation and coefficient algebra; not a generic image theorem

claims.statement: If H is polynomial, f divides Delta(H), and c is a nonzero constant, Delta+(c+Delta(H)/f)*d/dw has a slice iff H mod f belongs to k[x^5]. Equivalently Delta+(c+2r*h'(x))*d/dw has a slice iff h belongs to k[x^5].
claims.status: complete all-degree formal-orbit working proof with separate model reconstruction and exact supporting identities
claims.scope: all polynomial H satisfying the first-pole hypothesis for the specified Delta

claims.statement: For every a in k[x,f,g], Delta+a*d/dw has a polynomial slice iff a=c+Delta(H) for some nonzero constant c and polynomial H in k[x,y,z]; every positive case has a coordinate slice and polynomial kernel.
claims.status: complete full-coefficient-family working proof; separately reconstructed and adversarially reviewed by models
claims.scope: not all coefficients in k[x,y,z], not all four-variable LNDs, and not a solution to cancellation
claims.formalization: finite identity checks only; no full proof-assistant formalization

claims.statement: The primitive ansatz rP with P in k[x,f,g] is incomplete: S=x^2y+fz is polynomial and Delta(S)=5gx^2-4f^3x, which is not divisible by f.
claims.status: exact counterexample to a proposed restricted ansatz

claims.statement: For the displayed standard commuting slice family on the Koras-Russell cylinder, the algebra generated by its kernels is A[xw,zw,t^2w], which does not contain w.
claims.status: family-specific written calculation inspected separately; not a full invariant computation
claims.scope: does not show that the full modified Derksen invariant is proper

claims.statement: The December 2024 modified-Derksen paper explicitly leaves the Koras-Russell-cylinder distinction open and gives a full-ring versus proper-infinitely-generated dichotomy for nonrigid bases.
claims.status: known external theorem and source-version-specific open-problem statement
claims.scope: targeted later searches do not certify the absence of a subsequent resolution

claims.statement: For arbitrary a in k[x,y,z], a slice of Delta+a*d/dw implies a=c+Delta(H)/f^m for a nonzero constant c, polynomial H, and m>=0.
claims.status: complete working proof by localized normal forms and rescaled orbit moments

claims.statement: For the fixed Delta, a slice of Delta+(c+Delta(H)/f^m)*d/dw forces Delta(H)/f^m to be an actual polynomial Delta derivative, for every m>=1.
claims.status: complete higher-pole working proof, with two separate model audits finding no gap
claims.scope: uses fixed-base homogeneous degree, plinth, residue kernel, formal branches, and Weierstrass preparation; not formally verified

claims.statement: For every a in k[x,y,z] over a characteristic-zero field, the specified Freudenburg extension Delta+a*d/dw has a slice iff a=c+Delta(H) with c nonzero constant and H polynomial. Every positive case has explicit polynomial kernel coordinates.
claims.status: complete all-coefficient working proof, separately critiqued by models
claims.scope: all vertical coefficients for one fixed derivation; not a reduction of arbitrary slice LNDs and not a solution of Zariski cancellation
claims.formalization: finite exact checks only, not proof-assistant verification

claims.statement: If the fixed-family coefficient a has ordinary total degree at most four, a slice exists iff a is a nonzero constant.
claims.status: corollary of Z027 and homogeneous degree of Delta
claims.evidence: deep-pass-04.md section 1; independent degree-two moment proof in research/outside-coefficient-experiments.md

claims.statement: For arbitrary base LNDs the gauge criterion can fail: x^2*d/dy+(1+xy)*d/dw has the displayed nonlinear polynomial slice although xy is not in x^2*k[x,y].
claims.status: explicit exact counterexample to a proposed generalization, not to cancellation

claims.statement: If b is delta-invariant and delta(F)=b*a, exp((F-b*w)*(delta+a*d/dw)) conjugates d/dw to b*delta+(1+delta(F))*d/dw.
claims.status: general elementary conjugation lemma with written proof and finite exact inverse checks

claims.statement: The explicit nongauge affine-w slice over xy=z^2-1 reconstructs a polynomial cylinder isomorphism with x^2*Y=Z^2-1; the base is not a polynomial ring.
claims.status: reconstruction of known Danielewski cylinder phenomenon, with exact two-way inverse checks

claims.statement: Testing a-c in Delta(R) for rational polynomials is finite: only primitive components of degree at most deg(a)-4 need be considered, because Delta is homogeneous of degree four.
claims.status: elementary complete degree bound for the fixed derivation; computational resource limits must return unknown

claims.statement: For the same fixed-base family, properness of the additive-group action is equivalent to existence of a polynomial slice and to a being a nonzero constant plus a polynomial Delta derivative.
claims.status: working corollary of all-degree orbit proofs, separately audited by another model
claims.scope: one fixed rank-three base, not all proper actions on affine four-space

claims.statement: If K[s] is a four-variable polynomial ring over C and dim(K)=3, then K admits a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation.
claims.status: known one-variable rigidity theorem, independently reconstructed; corrects an earlier missed consequence

claims.statement: For K[s]=C[x1,x2,x3,x4], either a negative-s-degree coordinate partial proves K is polynomial, or the four top symbols induce commuting nonzero LNDs of K; generic rank three of these induced fields proves K is polynomial.
claims.status: complete elementary sufficient-condition proof using closed unipotent orbits on affine varieties
claims.scope: the generic-rank-three hypothesis is not proved in general and can fail for a chosen ambient coordinate system

claims.statement: Four independent commuting coordinate partials can have s-filtration leading symbols of generic rank one, even when K itself is a polynomial ring.
claims.status: explicit polynomial-inverse counterexample, checked exactly
claims.scope: counterexample to rank preservation, not to cancellation

claims.statement: Taking a lower horizontal coefficient, a commutator with d/ds, or an unlicensed projection to s=0 of a coordinate LND need not yield an LND.
claims.status: explicit coordinate-change counterexamples with nonterminating iterate formulas
claims.scope: specialization is valid when the derivation preserves the specialization ideal

claims.statement: For m,r,q>=2, P=x+x^m*y+z^r+w^q has smooth fibers but is not a slice of any LND and cannot become a coordinate after polynomial stabilization. Its fiber Euler characteristics are 1 at zero and 1-(r-1)*(q-1) elsewhere.
claims.status: complete elementary fiber-stratification proof, separately reconstructed
claims.scope: does not decide whether the abstract cylinder over the zero fiber is affine space

claims.statement: If B=K[s] is polynomial, then s is a coordinate in B[t] after adding one variable, because K[t] is isomorphic to K[s].
claims.status: elementary stable-coordinate reduction already present in the literature
claims.scope: descent to a coordinate of B remains unproved in four variables and would solve the target

claims.statement: Linearizing the s-dilation on K[s]=C^[4] is equivalent to proving K is polynomial; this torus action has complexity three, so complexity-two fixed-locus linearization results do not apply.
claims.status: elementary equivalence and statement-level source-scope check

claims.statement: A critical-point-free polynomial of degree at most two over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not two is a coordinate. In particular, every quadratic slice polynomial is a coordinate.
claims.status: complete elementary symmetric-matrix and triangular-coordinate proof

claims.statement: For a critical-point-free genuine cubic polynomial in four complex variables, its leading projective cubic surface is singular.
claims.status: complete elementary homogenized-gradient and height-theorem proof
claims.scope: necessary condition only, not a cubic slice classification

claims.statement: Kuroda's stable-invariant initial-form divisibility obstruction is automatically satisfied by every polynomial of total degree at most three in four variables.
claims.status: complete elementary factor-count and transcendence-degree argument
claims.scope: limitation of this necessary condition, not a positive stable-coordinate theorem

claims.statement: For F=x^2*y+g(x,z,w) of total degree at most three, F is a slice, a stable coordinate, or a coordinate exactly when a constant directional derivative of g(0,z,w) equals one.
claims.status: complete elementary cubic plane-curve proof and explicit inverse, separately reconstructed; coordinate criterion overlaps published work

claims.statement: For arbitrary g and m>=1, x^m*y+g(x,z,w) is a slice or stable coordinate exactly when g(0,z,w) is a plane coordinate; a finite inverse modulo x^m gives explicit positive coordinate formulas.
claims.status: working full proof with primary-source plane rectification; positive criterion is contained in Maubach's existing classification

claims.statement: For every nonzero p in C[x], F=p(x)*y+g(x,z,w) is a slice, stable coordinate, or coordinate exactly when every g(a,z,w) at a root of p is a plane coordinate.
claims.status: complete compact-cohomology necessity and published Maubach sufficiency; arbitrary degrees and root multiplicities
claims.scope: not a statement about arbitrary slice polynomials or cancellation of a single abstract zero fiber

claims.statement: For F=v^T(A0+x*A1)v+b(x)^T*v+c(x), with v in C^3, symmetric A0,A1 and determinant not identically zero, slice/stable-coordinate/coordinate are equivalent to critical-point-freeness and nonzero constant determinant.
claims.status: complete working Euler-characteristic obstruction and explicit nilpotent matrix-square-root inverse; two separate model audits found no gap
claims.scope: affine symmetric matrix pencil; arbitrary polynomial b and c; not a generic cubic classification

claims.statement: For symmetric polynomial A(x) with det A identically zero, every stable coordinate v^T*A(x)*v+b(x)^T*v+c(x) in four variables is a coordinate.
claims.status: primitive kernel vector completed over C[x] reduces to Z046 or the known three-variable stable-coordinate theorem

claims.statement: For every symmetric affine three-by-three matrix pencil A0+x*A1 and arbitrary polynomial b,c, the polynomial v^T*A(x)*v+b(x)^T*v+c(x) is a slice iff it is a stable coordinate iff it is a coordinate.
claims.status: working corollary combining full-rank Z047 and rank-deficient Z048
claims.scope: no reduction of all cubics or all slices to this family has been proved

claims.statement: For K[s]=C^[4], generically independent commuting LNDs of K have common kernel C[t] and only finitely many wholly rank-degenerate fibers; if the two fields are pointwise independent, K is C^[3].
claims.status: known special case of Derksen-van den Essen-Maubach Theorem 2.1; independently reconstructed here; degeneration remains an unproved exclusion
claims.scope: the required intrinsic pair and absence of bad fibers are not established in general

claims.statement: For every m>=2, F=x+x^m*u*v+w^2 has all fibers smooth with compactly supported Euler characteristic one, but Hc^3 of every nonzero fiber over Q is Q; F is not a stable coordinate or an LND slice.
claims.status: complete compact-cohomology proof, separately reconstructed; explicit algebra checked exactly
claims.scope: counterexample to an Euler-only test, not to cancellation or stable-coordinate descent; the abstract zero-fiber cylinder is not decided

claims.statement: For every quadratic P in three complex variables with rank-three quadratic part and every polynomial H, P*u+H is not a stable coordinate or an LND slice.
claims.status: complete rational obstruction for the smooth quadric and integral torsion obstruction for the cone; separate model reconstructions
claims.scope: no degree bound on H; a polynomial-map obstruction, not a general zero-fiber cancellation theorem

claims.statement: For F=(xy-1)*u+H, stability is equivalent to H(x,x^-1,z)=c*x^k*z+B(x), with c nonzero, k integral, and B Laurent; every positive case has an explicit polynomial coordinate inverse.
claims.status: complete all-fiber cohomology and tangent-direction argument; separately audited and inverse-checked

claims.statement: For F=xy*u+H, every stable coordinate is a coordinate. Nonconstant H(0,0,z) forces H=a*z+b+B(x)+C(y)+xy*K; constant H(0,0,z)=b forces, up to swapping x,y, H=a*y+c*x^k*z+B(x)+xy*K with a,c nonzero and k>=1.
claims.status: complete two-branch compact-cohomology classification with explicit polynomial inverses; separately reconstructed
claims.scope: arbitrary degree H; constants and polynomial normalizations specified in the appendices

claims.statement: For P in C[x,y,z] of degree at most two and arbitrary H in C[x,y,z], a stable coordinate P*u+H is an ordinary coordinate.
claims.status: complete working theorem combining exhaustive quadratic normalization, Z046, known three-variable stable descent, and Z052-Z054
claims.scope: includes zero and constant P; no degree bound on H

claims.statement: A genuine cubic stable coordinate F=f3+f2+f1+f0 in four complex variables has a projective point p with grad(f3)(p)=0 and f2(p)=0, using the Jacobian locus including nonreduced leading forms; a linear coordinate change therefore writes F=u*P(v)+H(v), deg P<=2, deg H<=3.
claims.status: complete projective Euler/Milnor obstruction, independently reconstructed with primary-source formulas

claims.statement: Every stable coordinate of total degree at most three in C[x1,x2,x3,x4] is an ordinary coordinate.
claims.status: complete working proof from Z041, Z055, and Z056; full-chain audit and proof-specific literature checks recorded separately
claims.scope: degree-bounded theorem, not unrestricted stable-coordinate descent or cancellation

claims.statement: If an LND on C[x1,x2,x3,x4] admits a slice of total degree at most three, its kernel is a polynomial ring in three variables.
claims.status: working corollary of Z057 and the standard slice theorem
claims.scope: the original cylinder hypothesis supplies no general slice-degree bound

claims.statement: For a stable coordinate F of degree d>=3 in four complex variables, the projective Jacobian locus V(partial(fd)) meets V(f(d-1)); after a linear change one chosen variable has partial degree at most d-2.
claims.status: same projective Euler/polar proof as Z056, with general-degree arithmetic independently checked
claims.scope: does not lower total degree; quartics reduce only to A(v)u^2+B(v)u+C(v) with coefficient degree bounds 2,3,4

claims.statement: For F=x^r*y^s*u+H over C, r,s>=1, with H(0,0,z) nonconstant, stability is equivalent to H=a*z+b+B(x)+C(y)+xy*R, a nonzero, B(0)=C(0)=0; every positive case has an explicit polynomial inverse.
claims.status: complete working all-exponent proof with independent reconstruction and two-sided finite-inverse checks
claims.scope: no degree bound on H; fixed-(x,y) inverse requires nonconstant intersection restriction

claims.statement: If a stable x^r*y^s*u+H has H(0,0,z)=b, then up to exchanging x,y and r,s, H=a*y+c*x^k*z+B(x)+xy*R, with a,c nonzero, k>=1, B(0)=b.
claims.status: complete working necessary-condition proof using integral Gysin residue, not just rational ranks or critical gradients
claims.scope: not an iff criterion for stable or ordinary coordinates with repeated coefficients

claims.statement: For r>=1,s>=2,q>=2, G=x^r*y^s*u+y+x*z^q has every fiber smooth with chi_c=1, but every nonzero fiber has ordinary H^0=Z, H^3=Z/q and all other cohomology zero; G is neither stable coordinate nor LND slice.
claims.status: complete working integral Gysin proof, independently reconstructed; residue degree checked exactly
claims.scope: cohomology formula only for nonzero fibers; not a cancellation counterexample

claims.statement: Every original LND slice F=x^r*y^s*u+H(x,y,z) in C[x,y,z,u], r,s>=1 and arbitrary H, is a coordinate and has polynomial three-variable kernel.
claims.status: complete working proof from Z060-Z061, the prior fiber theorem Z064, and the original slice decomposition; separately reconstructed
claims.scope: D(F)=1 must hold for an LND on the original four-variable ring, not just after stabilization; no claim every slice admits this form

claims.statement: For F=x^r*y^s*u+a*y+c*x^k*z+B(x)+xy*R, r,s,k>=1 and a,c nonzero, every quotient by F-lambda(x) is C[x]^[2]; the exchanged form has the analogous C[y] result.
claims.status: known special case of KVZ residual-plane Theorem 4.23; localized inverses and an independent PID-fibration reconstruction supplied
claims.scope: no stability needed for the fiber theorem; separate fiber polynomiality is not global coordinate completion of F

claims.statement: For stable H=s^2+G(v) in four variables, every G fiber is smooth and mod-2 acyclic; a general G fiber is integrally acyclic.
claims.status: applications of Smith theory and global Sebastiani-Thom, with exact primary hypotheses checked
claims.scope: does not prove contractibility, stable coordinate status, or polynomiality of G fibers; square completion from a quartic can give deg G=6

claims.statement: G in three complex variables is a coordinate iff H=s^2+G has, after some stabilization, an LND slice commuting with s->-s and fixing the other variables under that involution.
claims.status: complete conditional descent through the invariant ideal (s) and known three-variable stable-coordinate theorem
claims.scope: existence of this compatible LND does not follow here from ordinary stability

claims.statement: There is an explicit quartic coordinate H=s^2+x+y^4 and LND slice D(H)=1 whose average with its conjugate under s->-s is not locally nilpotent.
claims.status: complete explicit counterexample with all-iterate degree induction and exact identity checks
claims.scope: disproves averaging as a general repair, not existence of a different compatible slice

claims.statement: The standard commuting pair D1=2z*d_y-x^2*d_z, D2=3t^2*d_y-x^2*d_t on the Russell cubic is already saturated over C[x] in its C(x)-span but still loses rank modulo x.
claims.status: exact all-degree divisibility reconstruction on the known example; relation and independence identities checked
claims.scope: saturation need not remove every bad fiber under UFD/unit hypotheses; stable-cylinder status is not decided

claims.statement: The first Venereau polynomial xy^2*u+y+x^2*z+xy*z^2 has total degree four and is one-stable; its coordinate question is recorded unresolved in Blanc-Poloni 2022.
claims.status: primary source verified; no later resolution found in bounded search through September 12, 2026
claims.scope: current openness is not established by failure to locate a later result; known affine-space fibers do not solve the embedding question

claims.statement: For nonzero P in three complex variables, Hc^2(V(P)_red;Z) nonzero excludes stable P*u+H for every H. This applies to supports xyz and z(xy-1), with arbitrary positive factor multiplicities.
claims.status: complete working closed-open obstruction using a generic pure affine-curve center; explicit supports computed
claims.scope: necessary support test, not a classification of all cubic coefficients or a theorem about an individual zero-fiber cylinder

claims.statement: Every original LND slice F=(product_i ell_i^m_i)*u+H(x,y,z), for d>=2 distinct concurrent affine lines ell_i in the x,y plane and positive integer multiplicities, is a coordinate with polynomial three-variable kernel.
claims.status: complete working proof with independent reconstruction, using prior KVZ fiber descent; no degree bound
claims.scope: original four-variable LND slice required; no reduction of arbitrary slices or nonconcurrent arrangements to this presentation

claims.statement: For a central arrangement coefficient P=product_i ell_i^m_i with d>=2 and nonconstant H(0,0,z), F=P*u+H is stable iff H=a*z+B(x,y)+Q*R(x,y,z), where a is nonzero and Q=product_i ell_i. This form is a coordinate.
claims.status: complete working compact-support gluing proof and explicit finite inverse; independent exact checks
claims.scope: coordinates translated so the common line is x=y=0; criterion does not include the constant-axis branch

claims.statement: In the constant-axis central-arrangement branch, stability forces exactly one affine-line stratum and primitive radial maps on the other punctured-line strata; the resulting plane restrictions give every quotient by F-lambda(x) as C[x]^[2].
claims.status: integral residue image independently reconstructed; polynomial fiber conclusion is an application of prior KVZ Theorem 4.23
claims.scope: CRT only after inverting the distinguished x; coefficients of polynomial inverses have no other poles; not global stable-coordinate descent
claims.novelty: prior fiber theorem credited, not claimed

claims.statement: For F=h(s)+G(x,y,z), G=f(x,y)*z^q+g(x,y), deg h>=2, f nonzero and q>=1, F is stable iff G is a coordinate iff F is a coordinate.
claims.status: complete written deduction from global Sebastiani-Thom and binomial-surface rectification; independent reconstruction including constant and disconnected-fiber cases
claims.scope: no upper degree bound, but separated variables and binomial remainder required; deg h=1 cannot be included
claims.novelty: deduction from published results, no priority claim

claims.statement: If F=x*u^n+G(x,y,z), n>=2, is stable, then every G(0,y,z) fiber is A1, G(0,y,z) is a plane coordinate, and J=x*w+G is a coordinate preserving x in its completion.
claims.status: complete necessary-condition proof through a smooth rationally acyclic cyclic quotient; explicit two-sided quotient inverse
claims.scope: does not rectify the original cyclic cover or establish G as a coordinate over C[x]

claims.statement: The quartic coordinate F=x*u^2+y*u+x+z^4 has original LND slice D=partial_x-u*partial_y, but every fixed-x specialization has a critical point.
claims.status: explicit two-sided polynomial inverse, exact derivative and symbolic all-parameter checks
claims.scope: disproves absolute-slice-to-residual-x inference; not a cancellation counterexample and not in the x-divisible intermediate-coefficient subclass

claims.statement: The genuine quartic F=x*u^2+y+x^2*y^2 is critical-point-free and has G(0,y,z)=y and a polynomial cyclic quotient, but is not stable because its zero-fiber involution-fixed set is disconnected.
claims.status: exact gradient-ideal and factorization checks; written Smith-theoretic exclusion
claims.scope: necessary quotient condition and smoothness are not sufficient for stability; not a cancellation counterexample

claims.statement: For quartic F=x*u^2+B*u+C with x dividing B, polynomial square completion can produce a degree-five remainder; if x does not divide B, that square-completion substitution need not be polynomial.
claims.status: exact algebraic controls, including a degree-four coordinate whose remainder has degree five
claims.scope: does not preclude a different global coordinate change; records the limitation of the specified square-completion step

claims.statement: For G:C3->C with every fiber smooth and rationally acyclic, finite nonempty B containing all bifurcation values, T=H^2(general fiber;Z), and T_b=H^2(fiber b;Z), one has T^monodromy=0, H^1(C minus B;local system T)=direct sum T_b, and product |T_b|=|T|^(|B|-1).
claims.status: complete written Gysin-Leray deduction, separately reconstructed; finite cyclic-group arithmetic controls pass
claims.scope: forces integral acyclicity with trivial integral monodromy or constant torsion orders, not without those extra hypotheses; does not prove coordinatehood

claims.statement: Generic affine hypersurface fibers in C3 need not have torsion-free H1: the Dimca-Nemethi three-cuspidal quartic example has generic H1=Z/3 and monodromy -1.
claims.status: known primary counterexample, exact statement independently checked
claims.scope: its zero fiber is singular and generic Euler characteristic is four, so it is not a counterexample to the all-smooth-rationally-acyclic-fiber implication

claims.statement: For G=f(x,y)*z^q+g(x,y) over C, f nonzero and q>=1, a general smooth rationally acyclic fiber forces G to be a coordinate; a base automorphism makes f univariate, and for q>=2 gives f=p(a), g=b.
claims.status: complete written deduction with two model reconstructions from primary affine-modification lemmas and generic transversality
claims.scope: general fiber required, not one selected special level; q=1 does not make g a plane coordinate; no designated original variable is preserved

claims.statement: For nonzero A,B in C[x,y], C in C[x,y], and n,q>=2, F=A*u^n+B*z^q+C is stable iff it is a coordinate iff base coordinates a,b give C=b,A=r(a),B=p(a), with r,p nonzero univariate polynomials.
claims.status: complete written family proof with independent reconstructions and exact controls
claims.scope: no degree bound, but the two-pure-power presentation and two base variables are required; no arbitrary-slice reduction
claims.novelty: bounded statement audit only, no priority claim

claims.statement: For nonzero A,B in C[x,y] and positive exponents n,q, stability of A*u^n+B*z^q+C implies coordinatehood. The original-LND-slice kernel is therefore C^[3] in this family.
claims.status: complete written proof for exponents not both one, plus published KVZ Theorem 3.24 for the all-linear boundary
claims.scope: the stronger common-base classification is asserted only when both exponents exceed one; all-linear case credited to prior work

claims.statement: If p(a)*v^d+R(a,b,w) is a stable coordinate over C, p nonzero univariate and d>=1, then R(alpha,b,w) is a plane coordinate at every root alpha of p.
claims.status: complete smooth cyclic-quotient and rational Gysin proof; multiplicities, empty strata, and disconnected strata independently checked
claims.scope: necessary condition only for arbitrary d>1; no general cover-rectification converse

claims.statement: The quartic F=b+(a+b)^2*u^2+a^2*z^2 is critical-point-free and both cyclic fixed-surface polynomials are coordinates, but every nonzero fiber has Euler characteristic -3, excluding stability.
claims.status: explicit derivative-ideal identity and rational curve parametrization checked exactly; Euler obstruction proved in writing
claims.scope: counterexample to separate-fixed-plane-plus-smoothness criterion, not to cancellation; nonzero levels only in the displayed Euler formula

claims.statement: A nonconstant polynomial G in C[x,y,z] of degree at most three with general smooth rationally acyclic fiber is a coordinate. For d>=3, a smooth Euler-one fiber forces J(G_d) intersect V(G_(d-1)) nonempty and hence partial degree <=d-2 in a linear direction.
claims.status: complete written infinity and quadratic-rank proof; independent boundary-Euler reconstruction and exact arithmetic controls
